title: Where Is PostgreSQL Used?
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose and main terms of Where Is PostgreSQL Used.
Use or interpret an appropriate PostgreSQL example connected to web and mobile applications.
Identify one edge case and select a safe way to verify the expected result.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on Where Is PostgreSQL Used. Its primary job is to help you learn the PostgreSQL vocabulary and select a suitable database approach before writing queries. The listed PDF subtopics define the coverage expected here; work through them in order and connect each one to an example, edge case and checkable result.
content.why_it_matters: This topic matters because PostgreSQL systems must preserve correct results as data grows and more sessions or services interact with it. Practicing where is postgresql used? teaches you to make assumptions explicit, apply the right SQL or operational tool, and verify behavior instead of relying on a demonstration that only worked once.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Keep the problem small: learn the PostgreSQL vocabulary and select a suitable database approach before writing queries. A PostgreSQL feature should be chosen for the semantics it provides, not just because it is available. Before executing a change, state the inputs, expected output and boundary conditions. The example below is intentionally small enough to inspect; it illustrates the idea but is not a substitute for a test against your schema and PostgreSQL version.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Where Is PostgreSQL Used?
content_blocks.code:
SELECT id, name, price
FROM products
WHERE available IS TRUE AND price BETWEEN 1 AND 50
ORDER BY price, id
LIMIT 10;
content_blocks.expected_output: Returns up to 10 available products in the specified price range, ordered by price and then id.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Assumes products(id, name, price, available) with numeric price. Run against synthetic data.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For a read-only SELECT or inspection command, no reset is needed. For DDL/DML, use a disposable database; capture the starting state, run the example, inspect the result, and ROLLBACK or drop the lab objects as appropriate. Do not use production data or credentials.
content_blocks.limitations: CodeLeaf currently previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only; it does not execute PostgreSQL queries, shell commands or Python in the lesson page. Treat the sample as inspectable code unless you run it yourself in an approved isolated environment. Python examples require a separate isolated runner.
content_blocks.schema_assumptions: Assumes products(id, name, price, available) with numeric price. Run against synthetic data.

content_blocks.title: Practical checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Version note: PostgreSQL 18.6 is the primary reference. PostgreSQL 19 beta/development features are not assumed to be stable.

task: Create a short practice artifact for “Where Is PostgreSQL Used?”: explain its goal, show one example linked to “Web and mobile applications”, state the expected result, and include one edge/failure case and verification method. Use a disposable database or static artifact as appropriate.
hints: Start with the listed subtopics, especially “Web and mobile applications”, and describe the expected behavior in your own words.
Run or inspect the smallest example that demonstrates the behavior; do not add unrelated features before it is verified.
When the result surprises you, capture the exact SQL/error, check version and permissions, and change one assumption at a time.
expected_output: A reviewable note or query for Where Is PostgreSQL Used?, with an explanation of “Web and mobile applications”, expected behavior, and a documented edge-case check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying the example without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Object names, data types, privileges, extensions and data distribution affect database behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: List schema/version assumptions and test with a tiny synthetic dataset first.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a single successful query as proof of production readiness.
common_mistakes.why: A happy-path result does not test invalid input, concurrent sessions, permissions, recovery or query performance.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one negative/edge case and record the evidence that confirms the expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Making a production change directly from a lesson.
common_mistakes.why: DDL, data updates, role changes and operational commands can affect data or availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use an isolated lab, reviewed migration, least privilege, rollback/recovery plan and a second-person review for production.

summary: Where Is PostgreSQL Used? fits into the broader goal to learn the PostgreSQL vocabulary and select a suitable database approach before writing queries.
Use the curriculum subtopics as a completeness checklist: Web and mobile applications, E-commerce and multi-vendor platforms, Business and financial systems.
State the schema/version assumptions and verify one normal case plus an edge case before trusting the result.
